I found every egg room by myself, excluding Chapter 1. I looked for him in a Spamton Sweepstakes. I tried to help him, when it was day of love. And yet here Kris are. Not me, of course, that's not me, isn't it? Yet, it seems, we both looked for him. For Kris it might have been only a couple of days. And years of wait before, when this day happened. For me, it was almost a decade. Short meetings, so meaningful, yet isn't, all in between, when I was waiting for Deltarune, and Deltarune, waited for me.

And that's it? Only an egg? For so much wait? Was it meaningful at all? 

That's are stupid questions. Of course it was meaningful. Community effort, our memories, our thoughts, our headcanons. The man behind a tree will always remain a mystery in this dream. But would it be the same in my? In Kris's dream? In yours? I don't know! It's up to us. 

And yet, Kris felt, that we shall not seek for a man. Man said his last goodbye. And he left. As he was never been here. Or not? He really was always here, and always will be. As far as we remember him. We reached an end. But was ending a satisfying one? Well, it doesn't matter! All dreams, flower's dream, Knight's dream, Susie's dream, HIS dream, Kris's dream, our dream - all of them  were set to end. Which give them meaning. Without an end, there is no difference between dream and not-dream. So, if end is meant to differentiate states, what's  matters? All that's in-between. A path to end. We all left with much on our shoulders. Much great memory, countless nights of thought and connection. Connection with Kris, with Man, with other people in community. the often cited "first easter egg" in a video game was created by game programmer warren robinette, in the 1980 atari game "adventure." by following an obscure set of instructions, the player could discover his name in a hidden room. back then, common business practice was not to credit programmers or artists for games (in fact, atari was very against crediting any of the people who made their games possible). the only way warren robinette could be remembered was if he hid his name in that room. that room was the only place left he could speak.

im not sure what the egg rooms mean to toby fox, but i see them as a commentary on being an artist. how much of yourself do you put in your work? do you lose yourself in your creation, or hide yourself away where no one can find you? why do we make art, because it's therapeutic or because it's novel? even if it's just a trace of something you'd already seen before, the fact you made it, the fact it changed you irreparably, that makes it worth it. you can never wash it all away. you can never fully take away the artist from the art nor the art from the artist.

but your part in that, the viewer/reader/player's part in the communication that is art, is just as important. any art you consume will reflect something about you. you can't solely rely on what the author intended, because you can never know what the author intended. you can't look for easter eggs forever, but you can remember the artist as best you can.

I found every egg room by myself, excluding Chapter 1. I looked for him in a Spamton Sweepstakes. I tried to help him, when it was day of love. And yet here Kris are. Not me, of course, that's not me, isn't it? Yet, it seems, we both looked for him. For Kris it might have been only a couple of days. And years of wait before, when this day happened. For me, it was almost a decade. Short meetings, so meaningful, yet isn't, all in between, when I was waiting for Deltarune, and Deltarune, waited for me.

And that's it? Only an egg? For so much wait? Was it meaningful at all? 

That's are stupid questions. Of course it was meaningful. Community effort, our memories, our thoughts, our headcanons. The man behind a tree will always remain a mystery in this dream. But would it be the same in my? In Kris's dream? In yours? I don't know! It's up to us. 

And yet, Kris felt, that we shall not seek for a man. Man said his last goodbye. And he left. As he was never been here. Or not? He really was always here, and always will be. As far as we remember him. We reached an end. But was ending a satisfying one? Well, it doesn't matter! All dreams, flower's dream, Knight's dream, Susie's dream, HIS dream, Kris's dream, our dream - all of them  were set to end. Which give them meaning. Without an end, there is no difference between dream and not-dream. So, if end is meant to differentiate states, what's  matters? All that's in-between. A path to end. We all left with much on our shoulders. Much great memory, countless nights of thought and connection. Connection with Kris, with Man, with other people in community. And as his last goodbye, he give us something more, than just an egg. He gave us all this experience, all this love we put in him and in game. We certainly learned from man. 

And oh boy, does all that, flashing in my head on my first playthrough, accompanied with this. I haven't felt this sense of unity with the game, and Kris since one, similar moment, when Kris played the piano in Holiday house. And all this melancholy. Oh this left me in pieces. Kris is too now left with a weight on their shoulder. So, I think we were both touched. In a different manner of course, but nevertheless.

Thank you, forgotten man. I will never forget you.

Arguably, this Egg might be the easiest one to find. The other chapters have you going in and out of rooms or, in Chapter 3’s case, go to a convoluted series of actions that will mess you up if you don’t do them correctly. @khaos-inkarnatum yeah, the egg quest is really well designed. They cast a very wide net for the players, with chapter 3 being the “introduction” for people that truly leave no stone unturned and read every single line of dialogue with care, and chapter 5 for the people that notice the more intuitive easter eggs first. The quest isn’t hard to figure out at all, especially if you decide to cut your losses like a reasonable person and just look up the last step you have to do (that x wasn’t red when I first fought that damn frog I’m sure of it), but the cutting down of the wheat is just something instinctual. You CAN cut it all down, so obviously you MUST. There has to be a secret, right? 

Then the areas you get to themselves both serve as a great introduction. If you don’t have any eggs, the repeating line of trees clues you into the fact that there are more of them, and the music and tree should remind you a lot of the Scarlet Forest. In Chapter 3, you literally get told that there’s more and given (cryptic) instructions on how to get the other eggs. 

Anyways, if you’ve found one of these, and you’re the type of player that wants to experience all of the secrets, the rest aren’t that hard to find. I’d argue the first one is maybe a little too well-hidden. Like, I wouldn’t have figured that one out on my own, not on my first playthrough. It’s also a little too far away from the bake sale for me to consider it a truly “good” hint. The leap from “there is an invisible tree here” to “I need to repeatedly go back and forth to and from this area where previously was a bullet-throwing enemy” is a little too large imo and the Scarlet Forest is a lot bigger than that one room. I guess the music stopping and starting could be a clue but you need to back and forth a few times too many to figure that out organically. Like I’m pretty sure it is random and it took me the better part of five minutes last time. 

Anyways, holy yap. Just wanted to say that it’s pretty awesome how Chapter 3 and 5 both establish a starting point. I’m 100% sure Deltarune will do something with time-travel (as in, having to go back to replay old chapters) for something other than the eggs, I just don’t know what.
